title: Neuroplasticity: one study
stem: Section A short-answer question on the biological approach.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe one study that investigated neuroplasticity.
markscheme: aim of a relevant study identified, e.g. Draganski et al. (2004) investigated whether learning a new skill changes brain structure
procedure: e.g. participants learned to juggle for three months; MRI scans before, after learning and after a period without practice; control group did not juggle
results: e.g. grey matter increased in areas linked to processing visual motion in jugglers, and decreased again after they stopped practising
conclusion linked to neuroplasticity: the brain changes structurally in response to experience / use
Allow other relevant studies, e.g. Maguire et al. (2000) taxi drivers or Rosenzweig, Bennett & Diamond (1972)
parts.notes: Answers that only describe the brain area without a study's procedure or results should not get full marks. Evaluation is not required.

title: Schema theory
stem: Section A short-answer question on the cognitive approach.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain schema theory with reference to one study.
markscheme: schemas are mental frameworks of knowledge, built from experience, that create expectations
schemas influence encoding and retrieval, so memory can be reconstructive / gaps filled by expectations
relevant study described, e.g. Brewer & Treyens (1981): participants waited in an office and later falsely recalled schema-consistent objects such as books
explicit link: the study shows the office schema shaped recall / Allow Bartlett (1932) or Bransford & Johnson (1972) with a clear link
parts.notes: The link between the study and schema theory must be explicit for the final mark.
